_howTo: Copy this file to content/careers/roles/<role>.json (or, for one company only, to content/careers/overlays/<company>.json, see below) and fill it in. Then run: npm run seed:careers
role is the job role exactly as it appears on people, lower case ('graphics designer'). It is what a person's job role must match for their ladder to show.

rungs run from the entry level up. Rung 1 is where people start, so it never has steps. Rung N is level N (IC N on individual-contributor ladders, see content/careers/framework.json). Use 4 to 6 rungs.
Every rung says what that level looks like in the framework's three measures: knowledge, delivery, leadership. Write what you would see someone do, not adjectives.
steps are [track slug, level to pass]. Typical levels: IC2 5, IC3 8, IC4 10 to 12, IC5 12 to 16. A step on a track whose questions do not reach that level yet shows as 'coming soon' and never blocks.

bridges say where people on other ladders can cross into this one: someone who has reached fromLevel on fromRole can step into this ladder at toLevel. This is how 'junior developer to CTO' becomes a route.
Nothing here overwrites a ladder an admin has already edited in the app: seed:careers only creates ladders that do not exist, fills in blank wording, and with --add-steps adds steps that are missing.

_overlayFormat: A company that wants its own tracks on a shared ladder adds content/careers/overlays/<company>.json: { "company": "Moksy AI", "steps": [{ "role": "social media manager", "rung": 2, "slug": "moksy-brand-voice", "level": 5 }] }. These are added to the ladder, never replace it.
